title: Perfect verb tenses
subject: LANGUAGE
skillNames: Irregular Verbs with Has, Have, Had

slides.title: has and have
slides.text:
We use **has** or **have** + a special verb form to talk about things that happened **before now**.

**I have eaten** my lunch.
**She has seen** a camel.

slides.title: has or have?
slides.text:
**has**: he, she, it, one person or thing

**have**: I, you, we, they, two or more

**Ali has gone.** **The boys have gone.**

slides.title: Tricky verbs
slides.text:
Some verbs change a lot:

**see** → have **seen**
**eat** → have **eaten**
**go** → have **gone**
**write** → have **written**
**take** → have **taken**

proof.title: Prove it from the text
proof.text:
1. Find **who** did it. One person? Use **has**. More than one? Use **have**.
2. Look for clue words like **already**, **many times**, **just**, **ever**.
3. Use the special form: **seen**, not **saw**.

sentences.t: They have swum in the sea many times.

example.explain:
**They** means my brothers: more than one, so we use **have**.

**swim** changes to **swum**.

together.passage: Ali and his sister love animals. They ___ a camel many times. Today they want to see a lion.
together.stem: Which words fit best in the blank?
together.hint: They means two people. Is it has or have? And is it saw or seen?
together.good: Yes! Two people need have, and see becomes seen.

sentences: Ali and his sister love animals.
Today they want to see a lion.
evidence.stem: Tap 2 sentences: the one that shows there are two people, and the one with the clue many times.
evidence.wrong: This sentence is about today. Find who they are and the clue many times.

checks.passage: Sara is not hungry. She ___ her dinner.
checks.why: She takes has, and eat becomes eaten.

checks.passage: We ___ to the park three times this week.
checks.why: We takes have, and go becomes gone.

checks.passage: My dad ___ a letter to my teacher.
checks.why: My dad is one person, so has. Write becomes written.

again.title: Two parts
again.text:
This verb has **two parts**:

1. **has** or **have**
2. the special form: **seen**, **eaten**, **gone**

Never use **saw**, **ate** or **went** after has or have.
again.example:
**I have seen** the sea. (not have saw)

**He has eaten** dates. (not has ate)

slides.title: had + verb
slides.text:
Use **had** + a past participle (the past perfect) for an action that happened **before another past action**.

**When I arrived, the film had started.**

First the film started. Then I arrived.

slides.title: Same form for everyone
slides.text:
**had** is the same for every subject:

**I had**, **she had**, **they had**, **we had**

The participle is the same one you use with has/have: **had gone**, **had eaten**, **had written**.

slides.title: Clue words
slides.text:
Look for clues that show **two past times**:

**before, after, already, by the time, when**

**By the time we got home, it had begun to rain.**

proof.title: Prove it from the text
proof.text:
1. Find the **two past events**.
2. Decide which happened **first**.
3. The earlier event gets **had** + participle.

Point to the sentences that show the order.

sentences.t: Mona opened the oven at six o'clock.

example.explain:
The bread rose **first**. Mona opened the oven **later**.

The earlier action gets **had risen**.

together.passage: Yesterday, Omar woke up late. He ran all the way to the bus stop. When he got there, the bus ___. He had to walk to school in the heat.
together.stem: Which verb fits best in the blank?
together.hint: The bus left first, before Omar got there. Both happened yesterday.
together.good: Yes! The bus left before Omar arrived, so we use had left.

sentences: He ran all the way to the bus stop.
When he got there, the bus ___.
He had to walk to school in the heat.
evidence.stem: Tap 2 sentences that show this happened in the past and the bus was already gone.
evidence.wrong: This sentence does not show the time or that the bus was gone. Find the time word and what Omar had to do.

checks.passage: By the time we reached the beach, the sun ___.
checks.why: The sun set before we reached the beach. Set does not change: had set.

checks.passage: Lina could not get into the house. She ___ her key at school.
checks.why: She forgot the key before she tried to get in, so had forgotten.

checks.passage: After the guests ___ their coffee, they thanked the host.
checks.why: Drinking came first. Drink becomes drunk: had drunk.

again.title: Time line
again.text:
Draw a line. Put two dots for two past events.

1. The **left** dot happened first. It gets **had**.
2. The **right** dot happened later. It uses the simple past.
again.example:
• **The rain had stopped** ——— • **we went outside.**

Rain stopped first → **had stopped**.

slides.title: will have + verb
slides.text:
The **future perfect** shows that an action **will be finished before** a time in the future.

**By Friday, I will have finished my project.**

The project will be done before Friday arrives.

slides.title: Clues for the future perfect
slides.text:
Look for a future deadline:

**by tomorrow, by next week, by the time…, by 2030, before…**

**By the time the guests arrive, we will have cooked dinner.**

slides.title: Three perfect tenses
slides.text:
**has/have** + participle: before **now**
**had** + participle: before a **past** time
**will have** + participle: before a **future** time

proof.title: Prove it from the text
proof.text:
To choose the right perfect tense, find the **time clue**.

1. Is the deadline in the past, now, or the future?
2. Future deadline (by Friday, by next year) → **will have**.
3. Point to the sentences that give the time clue.

sentences.t: The new school opens in September.
By then, workers will have built twenty classrooms.

example.explain:
September is in the **future**. The classrooms will be finished **before** then.

So we use **will have built**.

together.passage: Huda joined a reading challenge this month. She reads twenty pages every evening. The book club meets next Friday to talk about the book. By then, Huda ___ the whole story. Her friend Reem started late and is still on chapter two. Reem hopes to catch up over the weekend.
together.stem: Which verb fits best in the blank?
together.hint: Is next Friday in the past or the future? The reading will be done before then.
together.good: Yes! Next Friday is in the future, and she will be done before it, so will have finished.

sentences: Huda joined a reading challenge this month.
She reads twenty pages every evening.
The book club meets next Friday to talk about the book.
By then, Huda ___ the whole story.
Her friend Reem started late and is still on chapter two.
Reem hopes to catch up over the weekend.
evidence.stem: Tap 2 sentences that show the future deadline.
evidence.wrong: This sentence does not give the future deadline. Find next Friday and By then.

checks.passage: By next summer, my brother ___ to drive.
checks.why: By next summer is a future deadline, so will have learned.

checks.passage: I can't play now. I ___ my homework yet.
checks.why: The action is not done before now, so we use have not (haven't) finished.

checks.passage: By the time the plane lands in Jeddah, we ___ for six hours.
checks.why: The landing is in the future, and fly becomes flown: will have flown.

again.title: Look for by
again.text:
The word **by** + a time is a big clue.

1. **By** + a past time → **had** + participle
2. **By** + a future time → **will have** + participle
again.example:
**By last night**, I **had finished** the book.

**By tomorrow night**, I **will have finished** the book.

slides.title: Choosing the perfect tense
slides.text:
All perfect tenses connect **two times**: an action and a reference point.

**Present perfect**: reference point is **now** (since, for, already, yet, ever)
**Past perfect**: reference point is a **past** moment
**Future perfect**: reference point is a **future** moment

slides.title: since and for
slides.text:
The present perfect often shows something that **started in the past and continues now**:

**She has lived in Riyadh since 2019.**
**They have studied English for five years.**

**since** + a starting point; **for** + a length of time.

slides.title: Keep tenses logical
slides.text:
In a passage, check that each perfect tense matches its time clue.

Wrong: **By next month, the team had finished the bridge.**
Right: **By next month, the team will have finished the bridge.**

proof.title: Prove it from the text
proof.text:
For each blank:

1. Find the **reference point** in the passage: now, a past moment, or a future moment.
2. Match it: **has/have**, **had**, or **will have**.
3. Use the correct participle (**begun**, **written**, **chosen**).

The sentences with the time clues are your proof.

sentences.t: The museum has displayed this old map since 1990.
Before it arrived, it had travelled across three countries.
By next year, more than a million visitors will have seen it.

example.explain:
**since 1990** → continues now → **has displayed**.

**Before it arrived** → earlier past → **had travelled**.

**By next year** → future → **will have seen**.

together.passage: Our class is creating a history project about our town. We (1) ___ on it since September, and each group has chosen a different topic. Before we started, most of us (2) ___ never ___ the old fort near the market, even though it is only a short walk from school. By the end of the year, we (3) ___ a model of the whole old town for the school exhibition.
together.stem: Which set of verbs correctly completes blanks (1), (2) and (3)?
options: (1) had worked (2) have … visited (3) will have built
(1) have worked (2) had … visited (3) will have built
(1) will have worked (2) had … visited (3) have built
(1) have worked (2) will have … visited (3) had built
together.hint: Find the time clue for each blank: since September, Before we started, By the end of the year.
together.good: Yes! since → have worked, before a past moment → had visited, by a future time → will have built.

sentences: Our class is creating a history project about our town.
We (1) ___ on it since September, and each group has chosen a different topic.
Before we started, most of us (2) ___ never ___ the old fort near the market, even though it is only a short walk from school.
By the end of the year, we (3) ___ a model of the whole old town for the school exhibition.
evidence.stem: Tap 2 sentences that contain a time clue for a blank.
evidence.wrong: This sentence introduces the project and has no blank. Find the sentences with since, Before or By the end of the year.

checks.passage: My grandmother ___ in the same house for fifty years, and she still loves it.
checks.why: For fifty years and still loves it show the action continues now: has lived.

checks.passage: By the time the firefighters arrived, the neighbours ___ the small fire with sand.
checks.why: Putting out the fire happened before the past moment when firefighters arrived.

checks.passage: Draft: By 2030, the city had planted ten million trees.
checks.stem: How should the verb be corrected?
checks.why: 2030 is a future deadline, so the future perfect is needed.

again.title: Find the anchor
again.text:
Every perfect tense is tied to an **anchor** time.

1. Find the anchor: **now**, a **past** moment, or a **future** moment.
2. Anchor = now → **has/have**
3. Anchor = past → **had**
4. Anchor = future → **will have**
again.example:
Anchor: **when the match started** (past) → The rain **had stopped**.

Anchor: **by the time you read this** (future) → I **will have left**.

Anchor: **now** → I **have finished**.
